title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: federated Copilot connectors read third-party data in real time
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting general documentation, qualify authentication requirements and clarify the control paths and API properties.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where a connector supplies the tools, Copilot can create, update or delete source data with user approval.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval.
claims.fix: After this description, add: "The broader connectors overview still calls federated connectors read-only, alongside a note that write actions would be available starting early October 2026; this briefing follows the dedicated federated connectors page." claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The source system limits reads and actions to the signed-in user's existing permissions.
claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions. Users can only access content they're authorized to view and make changes they're authorized to make in the original data source.

claims.claim: The source system remains the system of record.
claims.quote: The source system remains the system of record, and users can access only the data their account is permitted to access.

claims.claim: Source results reach the user's Copilot conversation.
claims.quote: Copilot selects relevant connector tools at runtime and uses the live results returned by the source to respond in the conversation.

claims.claim: Learn says administrators can audit federated connector activity in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The federated connector overview gives no audit path or connector-specific read and write event names.
claims.quote: Searched: federated Copilot connectors Purview audit event names connector reads writes; read federated-connectors-overview and purview/ai-m365-copilot. The overview states auditing exists but supplies neither an audit path nor event names.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The default on arrival of this government-cloud GA milestone is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "default" "general availability"; 569212 November 2026 federated connectors general availability rollout default. Read roadmap, overview, manage, custom setup and service description; conditional defaults do not specify this milestone.

claims.claim: Microsoft-built connectors are available when their publisher option is selected and users are included in User access.
claims.quote: Microsoft-built federated connectors are available by default when you select Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft in Agent and plugin access and include the user in User access.

claims.claim: External-publisher connectors require their publisher option to be selected or an administrator to turn on an individual connector.
claims.quote: Connectors from external publishers are available only when you select Allow agents and plugins built by external publishers, or when an admin turns on the individual connector.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Connector-specific sensitivity-label and data-policy enforcement on returned source data is not stated in the connector documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "sensitivity" "policies". Read federated overview, custom setup, prerequisites and Purview ai-m365-copilot; no connector-specific enforcement on returned MCP source data is stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview documents auditing Copilot prompts and responses.
claims.quote: Like other activities, prompts and responses are captured in the unified audit log.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview documents eDiscovery of Copilot prompts and responses.
claims.quote: Because user prompts and responses for AI apps are stored in a user's mailbox, you can create a case and use search when a user's mailbox is selected as the source for a search query.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview documents retention of Copilot prompts and responses.
claims.quote: Use retention policies to automatically retain or delete user prompts and responses for AI apps.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Users; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users sign in to each source with their own credentials.
claims.quote: User credentials, rather than admin credentials, are required to connect to any data source.
claims.fix: Qualify this as "Where a source requires authentication, users sign in with their own credentials." In Scope, qualify connecting to each source with "where authentication is required". In the impact rationale, replace "and sign in to the source" with "and, where required, sign in to the source". The cited custom setup page supports No Auth and says "Users don't need to authenticate".

claims.claim: The overview says OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication secure access and authentication.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.

claims.claim: Custom federated connectors support Microsoft Entra SSO, OAuth 2.0 and No Auth.
claims.quote: Custom federated connectors support three authentication methods. Choose the method that matches your data source.
claims.fix: After this sentence, add: "The broader connectors overview still marks custom federated connectors as unsupported; this briefing follows the dedicated custom setup page." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview#types-of-copilot-connectors, whose table says "Custom connectors | Yes | No | No".

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools default to Needs approval, which means Copilot asks for confirmation each time.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Always allow prevents further prompts for that tool until the user changes its setting or the publisher changes the tool.
claims.quote: Always allow | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A publisher-added or changed write tool is set to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools are part of the connector and are not enabled separately.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools are part of the connector and aren't enabled separately.

claims.claim: Publishers can add or change a connector's tools over time.
claims.quote: The actions available through a connector depend on the tools exposed by the connector publisher. Publishers can add or change tools over time.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Connector enable, disable and staging changes can take up to 10 minutes to take effect.
claims.quote: Changes can take up to 10 minutes to take effect across Microsoft 365 experiences. Refresh the admin center if staging changes don't appear.

claims.claim: Users might need to refresh Copilot after a control changes.
claims.quote: Users might need to refresh Copilot or start a new conversation.

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs MCP servers restricting source IPs to allow Copilot's static egress addresses.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Static egress is enabled by default for MCP-based federated connectors.
claims.quote: Static egress is enabled by default for MCP-based federated connectors.

claims.claim: The feature is included within the Microsoft 365 Copilot entitlement the page names.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.
